terminology.notes: New York uses Plaintiff/Defendant (NOT Petitioner/Respondent). The initiating document is a VERIFIED COMPLAINT (sworn under oath), not a petition. The court is the Supreme Court (the trial court of general jurisdiction for divorce), NOT Family Court. Case number is an Index No., not a Case No.

barriersStatement.notes: Must be served if married in religious ceremony

findingsOfFact.name: Findings of Fact and Conclusions of Law

serviceOfJudgment.name: Affidavit of Service by Mail of Judgment

options.additionalRequirement: Both parties were residents at commencement AND cause of action arose in NY
options.description: DRL § 230(1): Both parties are residents of NY when action commenced AND the cause of action arose in NY

options.additionalRequirement: Both parties domiciled in NY when action commenced
options.description: DRL § 230(2): Both parties are domiciled in NY at the time the action is commenced

options.additionalRequirement: Parties were married in New York OR cause arose in NY
options.description: DRL § 230(3): Plaintiff domiciled in NY for at least 1 year AND parties were married in NY OR cause of action arose in NY

options.additionalRequirement: Parties once lived as married couple in NY
options.description: DRL § 230(4): Plaintiff domiciled in NY for at least 1 year AND parties once lived as husband and wife in NY

options.additionalRequirement: Cause of action arose in NY AND either party has been domiciled in NY for at least 1 year
options.description: DRL § 230(5): Cause of action arose in NY AND either party has been domiciled in NY for a continuous period of at least 1 year immediately preceding the commencement of the action

options.additionalRequirement: Either party has been domiciled in NY for at least 2 continuous years
options.description: DRL § 230(6): Either party has been a domiciliary of NY for a continuous period of at least 2 years immediately preceding the commencement of the action

noFaultRequirement.description: For no-fault divorce, marriage must be irretrievably broken for at least 6 months

waitingPeriod.description: No mandatory waiting period after filing, but no-fault ground requires 6-month breakdown period

noFault.name: Irretrievable Breakdown
noFault.description: Relationship broken down irretrievably for at least 6 months
noFault.notes: Stated under oath in court papers

fault.name: Cruel and Inhuman Treatment
fault.description: Conduct endangering physical or mental well-being

fault.name: Imprisonment
fault.description: Confined in prison for 3+ consecutive years after marriage

conversion.name: Living Apart - Judgment
conversion.description: Lived apart per decree/judgment of separation for 6+ months (reduced from 1 year by Chapter 673, Laws of 2025)

conversion.name: Living Apart - Agreement
conversion.description: Lived apart per written separation agreement for 6+ months (reduced from 1 year by Chapter 673, Laws of 2025)

jointFiling.description: As of January 2025, couples can file jointly for uncontested divorce
jointFiling.notes: Separate packets available for with/without children under 21

automaticOrders.description: Automatic orders go into effect upon filing for Plaintiff and upon service for Defendant
restrictions: Cannot sell, transfer, or dispose of property without consent
Cannot remove children from state without consent

filingFees.notes: Fee waiver available for qualifying individuals

childSupport.description: In New York, child support generally continues until age 21

maintenance.incomeCapNote: Income cap of $241,000 for guideline calculations (effective March 1, 2026, CPI-U adjusted)
factors: Reduced earning capacity due to career sacrifice

propertyDivision.description: New York is an equitable distribution state. Marital property is divided fairly, not necessarily equally.
factors: Income and property at time of marriage and at commencement
Age and health of both parties
Need of custodial parent to occupy marital residence
Loss of inheritance and pension rights
Direct or indirect contribution to acquiring marital property
Liquid or non-liquid character of property
Difficulty of evaluating an interest in a business
Transfer of property made in contemplation of divorce
